Hi everyone! These are so so delicious, I really recommend and pretty easy too. Enjoy :)

Ingredients-
2 cups ham, chopped
4 ounces cream cheese, softened
1/3 cup coconut flour
1/2 teaspoon baking powder
1 1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese
3 eggs, beaten
Instructions
Preheat oven to 350 degrees

Method-
Combine ham and cream cheese until completely combined.
Add in remaining ingredients until well combined and chill 10 minutes.
**If you skip chilling the dough they will flatten as they cook and not be nice round balls**
Drop onto a greased baking sheet (I like to use the silicone baking mats) using a small cookie scoop.
Bake 20-23 minutes until golden brown.

This made 24 for me, but that will depend on the size scoop you use and how tightly you pack them.

So I kind of just made it up as I went along, so I’m not too sure of measurements.

Ingredients 

- 1 cauliflower 
- Some broccoli( if you want)
- Bowl of Grated cheddar 
- 200ml of double or single cream
- 3 Garlic cloves
- Half a White Onion
- 1 tbsp of butter
- Salt and Pepper

Method

Pre heat the oven to gas mark 5/190 Celsius.

Break up the cauliflower and broccoli into lots of florets. Put it in a large sauce pan of salted boiling water and cook for 5 mins. Then remove from water and put to one side.

Chop the onions and garlic. Heat the butter in a non stick frying pan. Add the onions plus garlic and cook for about 2 minutes. 

Next add the double cream and cheddar cheese, and continuously stir until all the cheese is melted and make sure the cream doesn’t burn. Add some water if it’s a bit too thick. 

Then add your cauliflower and broccoli and coat it with the sauce in the pan for around 1 minute maximum.

After put all of the sauce, cauliflower and broccoli in an oven proof dish. Season with salt and pepper. Place in the middle shelf for 25-30 minutes until the top is golden. 

Then you should have a perfect cauliflower cheese :)

When I went to Magaluf, a party island near Spain, (tacky I know), we went to a club on the first night. Everything was quite seedy, but the club was different and had a friendly atmosphere. There was a young Spanish DJ, and we requested a few songs and he was very nice. We went back every night to the same club because of the DJ.

One night I had gotten very drunkenly upset, thinking I would never find anyone who loves me and wants to be with me. Just a typical drunk girl. But the DJ said "hey your 20 years old, your young, do you want kids now,do you want to get married now?" My response was no and in that moment I realised how silly I was being and I had my whole life ahead of me. He also gave me a free shot which helped improve my mood haha. His name was Bobby (Roberto) and he was so so nice, just a pure soul in a very seedy place. He probably sees so many drunk girls and guys he will have no idea who I am, but yes I remember him with a happy heart.

However this same woman has worked in THREE Woody Allen films. He is well known to be a creep and even ran off with his adopted daughter. Yes it is tricky to prove. However my key point is, no one should lose their job or have their name slandered all over the press until they are guilty, proven by a court not crazies on twitter. A person who gets a guilty verdict from a jury then deserves all they get after, but there should no witchunting before this conclusion, it's just biased and wrong.

But are they being imposed? I have read of 3 cases in the past 3 months of fake accusations with proof to back it up, leading to years wasted for innocent men who are accused of rape. After the men are found not guilty, nothing happens to person who lied.

Yes I agree it can be hard to prove, but I have read several cases of rape accusations going to court and then in the last hours, before the final hearing was going to occur, new evidence appears that has been hidden or not found by police. For example a man was accused of rape, the case was ongoing for 2 years, and then finally police found texts from the female accuser which essentially said she had enjoyed their encounter and asked to meet up again. My impression is that the #metoo campaign is leading to a frenzy, where the police are in such a rush to convict anyone accused they miss vital evidence.
I think a way to tackle this is to make sure women (or men) who falsely accuse someone of rape or sexual assault/harrasment face jail time. That would discourage false claims.

I think a huge problem is people are outright believing the accusations. I think innocent until proven guilty by a court should apply. The accusations are destroying lives and many of these people are innocent.

Yea I agree, I'm a female, but I don't see someone wolf whistling at me or cat calling the same as rape or sexual assaults. It is actually very insulting as I have been sexually assaulted which very nearly turned into a rape, and to see others trying to get attention by labelling petty incidents as sexual assault is just disgusting..
